newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA STILL OPTIMISTIC ON OIL REVENUES.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA STILL OPTIMISTIC ON OIL REVENUES.

text.p: Venezuela's government is optimistic about oil revenues this year and expects them to come in $700 million over budget, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos said on Monday.

So far this year, the average export price of Venezuela's crude oil and refined products has been $16.59, and Matos expected it to stay above $16 for the whole year, against a budgeted $15 per barrel.

"That is a saving of one dollar which means $700 million in fiscal revenues. If this is the case, we will ask Congress for additional credit to fulfil public-sector wage rises and pay debt," he said at a third anniversary for Venezuela's tax superintendency SENIAT.

Venezuela exports about one billion barrels of crude oil and refined products per year and every dollar increase in price translates to 67 cents in taxes, royalties and dividends for the public purse.
Matos also said he expected public-sector wage increases to cost $15 billion, $5 billion more than official estimates up to now.
